issues.title: test(a11y): AT-SPI role and name mapping conformance — every accessibilityRole reaches an AT-SPI role
issues.body:
## Context

Accessibility is small in the `react-native-macos` tracker only because AppKit does the work — and even so:

- [rn-macos#266](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/266) — "Accessibility props for macOS need to be normalized with core": the platform invented its own
  prop names and had to be reconciled.
- [rn-macos#1359](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/1359) — VoiceOver does not localise some of the roles they claim to support.
- [rn-macos#1349](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/1349) and [rn-macos#1607](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/1607) — accessibility *commands* and custom actions never investigated.
- [rn-macos#428](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/428) — `<Image>` is inaccessible unless `accessible={false}`, which is backwards.
- [rn-macos#2645](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/2645) — open, 2025-08: accessibility traits still unshimmed under Fabric, years after the migration.
- [rn-macos#1348](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/1348) — VoiceOver announces "No selection" for the first `FlatList` item.

ADR-0001 is blunt about our position: AT-SPI2 over D-Bus is "a mapping from React Native's
`accessibilityRole`/`accessibilityLabel` props that has no upstream precedent to copy", and Flutter's own
direct-AT-SPI proposal has been open and unfinished since November 2024.

The lesson from macOS is narrow and useful: the *mapping table* is the artefact that rots. Roles get added
upstream, the platform table does not grow, and nobody notices because no test enumerates it.

## What to verify

1. Every value React Native's `accessibilityRole` accepts maps to a named AT-SPI role, or to an explicitly
   recorded "no equivalent" with a fallback — and the test enumerates the values from the upstream type, so a
   new upstream role fails the build.
2. `accessibilityLabel`, `accessibilityHint`, `accessibilityValue` and `accessibilityState` reach the
   corresponding AT-SPI properties and state set.
3. Focus and caret changes emit the corresponding AT-SPI events (the ADR names these explicitly).
4. `accessible={false}` removes a node from the tree; an image with a label is present, not absent
   ([rn-macos#428](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/428)).
5. The exposed tree is the *painted* tree — clipped-out and `zIndex`-covered nodes are ordered the way a
   screen reader should traverse them.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Unit (C++):** the role and state mapping tables, driven by an enumeration of the upstream prop values, at
  100% line and branch. Adding a role upstream must fail this test.
- **E2E:** an AT-SPI client attached over D-Bus under the headless compositor, walking the tree of a fixture
  bundle and asserting roles, names and the focus event sequence.

## Related

Scoped inside #27 (AT-SPI groundwork), which owns the implementation. This issue owns the enumeration and the
conformance test that keeps the table honest.

issues.title: feat(core): Modal and overlay surfaces — decide xdg_popup versus in-surface overlay
issues.body:
## Context

[rn-macos#481](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/481) — **open since July 2020, 6 reactions, 22 comments: "Modal not implemented".** It is the most
reacted open bug in the repository and it has been open for six years. [rn-macos#479](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/479) (14 comments) and
[rn-macos#1701](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/1701) ("[Fabric] Disable RCTModalHostViewComponentView for Fabric") are the same hole from other angles.
[rn-macos#604](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/604) and [rn-macos#617](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/617) (5 reactions) ask the adjacent question — multiple windows and desktop window APIs —
and were closed without an answer.

The reason it stayed open for six years is that it is a *decision*, not a feature: a modal is either a real
platform window with its own lifecycle, focus and stacking, or a subtree painted above everything inside the
existing surface. Each choice is cheap once made and expensive to change.

For us the fork is sharper. An `xdg_popup` is grab-based, positioned relative to a parent, dismissed by the
compositor and constrained by `xdg_positioner` — correct for menus, wrong for a full-screen dimmed modal. A
second `xdg_toplevel` is a real window the compositor may tile, which on Hyprland is emphatically not what a
React Native `Modal` means. An in-surface overlay costs nothing extra to composite in a retained scene we
already own — which is the argument the GPU-canvas architecture makes for itself.

## What to verify / decide

- Write the decision down first: in-surface overlay for `Modal`, with `xdg_popup` reserved for future menu
  and tooltip work. If that is the answer, this issue is small; if it is not, it needs an ADR.
- Overlay stacking above all content regardless of `zIndex`, with its own hit-test layer that blocks
  everything beneath (the [rn-macos#914](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/914) failure mode applies directly).
- Focus is trapped inside the overlay while it is open, and restored to the previously focused node on close.
- `onRequestClose` fired on Escape and on a compositor close request.
- `transparent`, `animationType` and the backdrop dim are paint concerns and land as goldens.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Decision recorded** in `docs/cpp-toolchain.md` (or an ADR if it is not the in-surface answer) before any
  code.
- **Unit (C++):** overlay stacking, hit blocking, and the focus trap/restore at 100% line and branch.
- **Golden-image:** an open modal over content, transparent and opaque backdrops.
- **E2E:** open, Tab through the trapped focus set, Escape to close, assert focus restored to the original node.

## Related

Depends on the focus model issue in this batch. Carries `needs:decision`. Deliberately M5 (multi-window and
hardening) rather than M1: ADR-0001's minimal surface is six components and `Modal` is not one of them.

issues.title: feat(input): secondary-button and context-menu event — a right click is not a left click
issues.body:
## Context

- [rn-macos#379](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/379) — closed, 4 comments: "Right clicking on Button and other Touchable based components is
  triggering the action as if it were a left click." The most basic desktop expectation, violated.
- [rn-macos#2085](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/2085) — closed, 5 comments: right-click context menu.
- [rn-macos#1209](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/1209) — closed: click handling breaks entirely after a context menu is opened over a `TextInput`.
- [rn-macos#754](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/754) — right-click hit region wrong on selectable text.
- [rn-macos#492](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/492) — closed: no API to add menu items.

`docs/cpp-toolchain.md` describes `PointerRouter` as "a mouse state machine and nothing more: which buttons
are down, which node the press started on, and therefore whether a release is also a click", and notes that
`click` is the platform's synthetic call. Nothing there distinguishes buttons, so a secondary-button release
on the press target is currently as much a `click` as a primary one — which is [rn-macos#379](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/379) exactly.

Only the event half of the macOS lesson transfers: Wayland has no menu bar and no system context menu, so the
menu itself would be ours to draw and is out of scope here.

## What to verify / build

- `BTN_RIGHT` and `BTN_MIDDLE` carry `button`/`buttons` in the pointer payload and do **not** synthesise
  `click` ([rn-macos#379](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/379)).
- A secondary press-and-release on a node emits `contextMenu` in the shape upstream's
  `PointerEventsProcessor` expects, so `onContextMenu` works where React Native supports it.
- Middle click pastes the primary selection into a focused editor rather than clicking (see the clipboard
  issue in this batch).
- Button state is per-button: a primary press held while a secondary press occurs does not lose the primary
  press target ([rn-macos#1209](https://github.com/microsoft/react-native-macos/issues/1209)).

## Acceptance criteria

- **Unit (C++):** `PointerRouter` button-state tests at 100% line and branch — each button's press/release
  pairing independently, interleaved presses, and the assertion that only the primary produces `click`.
- **E2E:** injected secondary and middle button sequences, asserting the trace contains no `topClick`.

## Related

Follows #18. Depends on the clipboard issue in this batch for middle-click paste. Menu drawing is explicitly
not in scope.
